rationale: The Latin anchors "odor" and "odoramen" (a scent/fragrance) point directly to the physical sensation or quality of a smell, and the Biblical citation "odoratus est Dominus odorem suavitatis" (the Lord smelled the sweet savour, Gen. 8:21) confirms a concrete, perceptible scent rather than the faculty of smelling or an abstract atmosphere. This aligns with smell.n.01, the sensation/stimulus from olfactory receptors.
